{{Orphan|date=July 2019}}

In mathematics, a '''Γ-object''' of a [[pointed category]] ''C'' is a [[contravariant functor]] from Γ to ''C''.

The basic example is [[Graeme Segal|Segal]]'s so-called '''Γ-space''', which may be thought of as a generalization of [[simplicial abelian group]] (or simplicial abelian monoid). More precisely, one can define a Gamma space as an O-monoid object in an infinity-category.<ref>{{harvnb|Lurie|loc=Remark 2.4.2.2.}}</ref> The notion plays a role in the generalization of [[algebraic K-theory]] that replaces an [[abelian group]] by something [[higher object|higher]].
